messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Erroneous sleep data returned from low activity signal
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Erroneous sleep data returned from low activity signal
messages.body_plain:
Hi Phil,

Sorry, I have ignored all GGIR e-mail traffic for a couple of months to focus more on new developments.
What you saw is the imputed data. This is clarified in the visualisation of part2, while non-wear time is not visualised at the moment in the other visualisations produced by GGIR.
When you are unsure about whether to include or exclude data always look out for variables related to non-wear time or valid hours, rather than judging the data on the plausibility of its value alone. Additionally, it is good checking out the calibration error reported in the part2 output.

Cheers,

Vincent

For all nights during the "bad" period, we get the exact same sleep/wake up detection periods displayed between approximately midnight to 8am night after night. Any idea what would be causing this problem? We will of course ignore these nights from our analyses, but are wondering why an exact pattern repeats itself.

> Hi Vincent,
>
> Thank you so much for developing this very helpful package. I have been using it with Actigraph data and it is really helpful. In the process I found two bugs that may be easily fixed.
>
> In g.inpectfile, line 138:
> tmp3 = as.character(unlist(strsplit(tmp2, "yy.at <http://yy.at>."))[2])
>
> It is limited by the format of the date (it has to be the format */*/yyyy). Instead, this may work:
> tmp3 = as.character(unlist(strsplit(tmp2, ".at.",fixed = T))[2])
>
> Then in g.getstarttime, line 119-126, the same problem occurs with different date format specification. If data formats other than */*/yyyy could be included, i.e. yyyy/mm/dd (the thousands of data files that I have are unfortunately in this format), that would be great.
>
> Thank you again for your hard work!
>
> Best,
> XInyue
>

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Selecting the correct amount of days and nights
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Selecting the correct amount of days and nights
messages.body_plain:
Hi Robin,

I see what you mean, but I am afraid GGIR as it is as the moment can only provide an approximation of this:
strategy = 2 will ignore the first day of measurement until midnight
and maxdays = 7 will ignore all measurement after 7 x 24 hours of data.

If you think this should be facilitate then:
- Create an issue on: https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/issues

messages.body_plain:
So my problem was coming from how the time and date were encoded. Our data comes from Los Angeles, so we needed time in PST. Look at the source code for part 5  and run it line by line you will notice when the error occurs. I had to write a gsub() around my date\time to make it compatible with the character input of date and time ( getting rid of timezone and T in between date and time). I am not posting the source code since this is a local solution and might not work for general public and I don't want to confuse people) but I changed the code for time on line 133 to  time = gsub("-0800","",gsub("T"," ",IMP$metashort[,1])).

Then I saved the file as g.part5.R in my local working directory and ran the following in my script before the g.shell.GGIR():

source("~/g.part5.R")
> assignInNamespace("g.part5",g.part5,ns="GGIR")
> source('~/getfolderstructure.R')
> source('~/identify_levels.R')

Hope this helps (download the source code from github)

messages.subject: GGIR version 1.6 with new qwindow functionality and faster Actigraph csv reading
messages.subject_clean: GGIR version 1.6 with new qwindow functionality and faster Actigraph csv reading
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I have uploaded GGIR version 1.6 to CRAN today. This should be available for download in the upcoming days. It comes with quite a few significant updates:

1. Part5 had a timezone dependent error, visible to some users as an error message with the text 'timebb[s0]...'. This bug has now been fixed.

2. The speed with which GGIR can read csv files from ActiGraph is much faster now and comparable to the speed with which binary data can be read from other accelerometer brands.

3. Argument qwindow is now able to handle input vectors longer than 2 and will derive all part2 variables for each time window that can be defined from the values of qwindow, e.g. value =c(0,8,24) will analyse the windows: 0-8, 8-24 and 0-24 hour. It will always consider the full 24 hours even if this is not specified with qwindow.

4. Because of #3, I deprecated argument L5M5window because argument qwindow now defines the window over which L5M5 analysis is performed.

5. Because of #3 I renamed some of the part2 output variable names to be more consistent in structure and more explicit about the time window over which they are calculated. The variables that were calculated over the full recording (using diurnal normalisation) now have the extension "fullRecording", this in contrast to the variables that are only calculated from measurement days with 'enough' valid data. Most of the 'fullRecording' variables have been in the part2 output for many years, and with all the new variables being added it was time to make their meaning more explicit. I apologise for the inconveniences these name changes may cause, but I hope you understand.

6. Argument winhr is now reflected in g.analyse/g.part2 output variable names, previously this variable name was hardcoded as L5M5, even if winhr was not set to 5 hours.

7. The calculation of N valid WEdays and Nvalid WKdays in part2 that was wrong since version 1.5-21 has now been fixed. It counted all days and did not exclude days with insufficient amount of data.

8. Because of #3 I felt that it was a good moment to also make a much needed update to output variables acc_timeinbed and acc_dur_noc in part4: I renamed acc_timeinbed to acc_SptDuration to avoid confusion with terminology used in the supporting papers (2015 and a second one hopefully soon), which are about SPT (sleep period time) detection and not about time in bed detection. Output variable acc_dur_noc has been renamed to acc_SleepDurationInSpt to improve clarity that it calculates the sleep duration within the Sleep Period Time as defined by acc_SptDuration.

Best wishes, Vincent
